currentContext.expansion: AIS describes FY 2025-26 as the closing year of the largest investment cycle in its history, with capital expenditure of Rs 666.26 crores during the year. The cycle comprised the third float-glass plant at Soniyana (Rajasthan), a float line cold repair at Roorkee, the Phase 2 expansion at Patan, and the on-site assembly facility at Kharkhoda, which together added significant capacity and capability. The new Soniyana float glass plant was commissioned during the year and, together with the Roorkee refurbishment, is expected to add to overall financial performance from next year; the Soniyana commencement strengthened vertical integration, localisation, inventory optimisation and supply-chain resilience. Brownfield investment continued at Patan, Chennai and Bawal, with Patan Phase 3 work started and Phase 4 implementation initiated - a phased approach that aligns capacity expansion with demand, technology and productivity requirements. Assembly operations at Nashik (Maharashtra) were expanded and ASN-Nashik was commissioned in FY 2025-26. Management characterises FY 2025-26 as a year of transition from building capacity to absorbing capacity, from commissioning assets to stabilising them, and from undertaking capital expenditure to improving the returns generated by it. Funding was supported by a Rs 1,000.00 crores QIP completed in 2025, the third capital raise in AIS's history, while total debt was reduced to Rs 2,058.67 crores with debt-equity improving from 0.96x to 0.52x. Separately, the downstream businesses ADSL, AIA and GX were merged into AIS Glass Solutions Limited, subsequently renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited, consolidating the consumer-facing entities.

risks.note: Three downstream subsidiaries (AIS Adhesives, AIS Distribution Services and GX Glass Sales & Services) were amalgamated into AIS Glass Solutions Limited under an NCLT-approved composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1st July, 2025, and the transferee was renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited. Consolidating several operating entities into one carries integration and execution exposure.

risks.risk: Emergence of a material subsidiary shifting exposure below the listed entity
risks.note: The Company had no material subsidiary in FY 2025-26, but AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited has been identified as a material subsidiary during FY 2026-27 on the basis of its financial statements. A growing share of value will sit in an entity whose results are not visible in the standalone accounts.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Asahi India Glass Limited (AIS) is India's leading integrated glass manufacturer, holding approximately 80% market share in the Indian passenger car glass segment.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: AIS manufactures and processes glass across three Strategic Business Units - Automotive Glass, Architectural (Building & Construction) Glass and Consumer Glass. It runs an integrated network of float glass plants, automotive glass processing facilities, architectural glass processing units and sub-assembly locations across India, supplying laminated windshields, tempered sidelites and backlites, sunroofs and encapsulated glazing to domestic and global OEMs, and float, coated, reflective, mirror, insulated, security and acoustic glass to the architectural market. end_markets.body:

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Improved demand in both automotive and architectural segments made FY 2025-26 a satisfactory year, with financial and operational performance largely close to budgets
- Indian vehicle production increased to 3.47 crore units in FY 2025-26 from 3.10 crore units in FY 2024-25, making India the third largest producer globally, with robust domestic demand supported by low finance rates and rising incomes
- Rapid electrification: registrations of electric passenger vehicles rose approximately 80% in FY 2025-26, supported by FAME policies and expanding charging infrastructure; EVs and premium ICE …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: AIS describes FY 2025-26 as the closing year of the largest investment cycle in its history, with capital expenditure of Rs 666.26 crores during the year. The cycle comprised the third float-glass plant at Soniyana (Rajasthan), a float line cold repair at Roorkee, the Phase 2 expansion at Patan, and the on-site assembly facility at Kharkhoda, which together added significant capacity and capability. The new Soniyana float glass plant was commissioned during the year and, together with the Roorkee refurbishment, is expected to add to overall financial performance from next year; the Soniyana …

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Dominant automotive glass position - approximately 80% share of the Indian passenger car glass segment, held with a healthy new-business win ratio
- Vertical integration from float glass manufacture through downstream value-added processing, strengthened by the third float plant at Soniyana
- Deep Localisation / 'QJCI' (Quality of Japan, Cost of India) model combining AGC group technology with Indian cost structures and in-house product design
- Proximity manufacturing: 15 plants and 11 sub-assembly units-cum-warehouses located near automotive and real-estate markets enabling just-in-time delivery, …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Board confirms there was no change in the nature of business during the year, and the reporting boundary covers only the Auto Glass, Architectural Glass and Consumer Glass SBUs. With no non-glass activity, a downturn in glass demand or glass economics has no offset elsewhere in the portfolio.
- The Directors' Report attributes the year's satisfactory performance directly to improved demand in both the automotive and architectural segments, so earnings are levered to two cyclical end-markets and to the OEM customers behind them.
- The reporting scope covers pan-India operations only, with manufacturing, processing and warehousing sites concentrated in India. There is no overseas manufacturing base to buffer a domestic demand or policy shock.
- The Board's Statement of Responsibility states that the Report contains forward-looking statements based on current assumptions, industry conditions and the Company's strategic plans, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual outcomes to differ materially, and that AIS undertakes no obligation to update them.
- Three downstream subsidiaries (AIS Adhesives, AIS Distribution Services and GX Glass Sales & Services) were amalgamated into AIS Glass Solutions Limited under an NCLT-approved composite Scheme of Arrangement effective 1st July, 2025, and the transferee was renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited. Consolidating several operating entities into one carries integration and execution exposure.
- The Company had no material subsidiary in FY 2025-26, but AIS Consumer Glass Solutions Limited has been identified as a material subsidiary during FY 2026-27 on the basis of its financial statements. A growing share of value will sit in an entity whose results are not visible in the standalone accounts.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Value-addition as the core lever: pursue superior value-added products, more efficient assets, sharper market segmentation and reliable service rather than relying on external trade remedies - value addition is a stated core strategic aim and a direct lever for margin improvement in architectural glass
